title: Grade 5 Social Studies — Foundations of U.S. Government
subject: Social Studies
description: Practice with questions on Constitution, separation of powers, rights, federalism.
creator: Teach Arcade

questions.question: What is the main job of the U.S. Constitution?
choices: sets store prices in every state
sets out how the federal government works
announces the first battles of the Revolution

questions.question: Which branch of the federal government makes laws?
Which branch carries out federal laws?
Which branch decides court cases about federal laws?
Which two bodies form the U.S. Congress?
What name is given to the first ten amendments?
What is an amendment?
choices: an official change or addition to the Constitution

questions.question: Residents write to Congress asking it to change a law. Which First Amendment freedom does this illustrate?
choices: the right to serve on a jury
the right to run for every office
the right to petition the government
the right to own a home

questions.question: What does it mean that the president can veto a bill?
choices: The president can write laws without Congress in every case.
The president can appoint every governor.
The president can reject a bill passed by Congress.
The president can erase all court decisions.

questions.question: Which is an example of a check on government power?
choices: A city mayor can replace Congress.
Every branch approves its own powers without limits.
The same person runs every branch for life.
Congress can override a presidential veto with enough votes.

questions.question: What does federalism divide power between?
Which power is assigned to the federal government?
choices: set hours for a local playground

questions.question: Which action most clearly involves a state power?
choices: setting rules for state driver's licenses

questions.question: Why are elections important in a representative system?
choices: Eligible voters can choose people to act for them.

questions.question: What earlier national frame of government preceded the U.S. Constitution?
What is one role of the U.S. Supreme Court?
choices: write all federal laws from scratch

questions.question: Which document announced independence, rather than setting up today's three federal branches?
What idea is introduced by “We the People” in the Constitution?
choices: There can be only one branch.
States have no people of their own.
Government authority is based on the people.
The president alone is the source of all laws.

questions.question: Why separate power among the branches?
choices: so every branch has exactly the same tasks
to limit the power any one branch can use by itself

questions.question: What source should you use first to check which branch has a named constitutional power?
choices: a physical map of North America
the text of the U.S. Constitution
